items.topic: Known non-issues added to reader prompt
items.claim: Readers repeatedly flagged `${java.version}` in POMs and the release-judong profile pointing at the snapshots URL as bugs.
items.fact: Opus validators rejected both several times. `${java.version}` is resolved by Maven from the running JVM. The `release-judong` profile pointing its release repository at the snapshots URL is deliberate: 98 judo-ng POMs do it, and swagger-p2 AGENTS.md:116 says release-judong deploys 'snapshots and releases'. The agent added both, plus empty EVL placeholders and Handlebars `{{#each ... as |x|}}` scoping, to reader-prompt.md as 'Known NON-issues (do not report)'.
items.evidence: session 2026-11-04T19:01, agent; validators C285-C287, C299, C302

items.topic: Subagent batch loop: round.py, splitting, failures
items.fact: The judo-ng-read sweep runs with `NREAD=21 NVER=24 python3 round.py`. Readers are `judo-ng-reader` subagents on model @explore and read reader-prompt.md with {ID}. Validators are `judo-ng-validator` on @validate and each handle 6 batch ids, writing out/<ID>.validate.json. check_batch.py accepts or rejects each out/<ID>.json. A batch with 'no output' is split automatically (C353 became C353a/b, C381 became C381a/b). Subagents sometimes fail with 'produced no final output'. Some write no file and ask for permission, for example C396, or answer in another language (C395). Those batches have to be re-queued, and the round.py state in queue-state.json can be repaired by hand: set the lost batches to 'accepted' and drop stale 'running' entries.

items.topic: Model proxy outage
items.fact: If subagents fail suddenly, probe the proxy with two trivial Agent calls: subagent_type proxy-test, models @explore and @validate, prompt 'Reply with exactly: OK'. The proxy had a temporary credentials error and then recovered.

items.topic: Validator pass rule
items.fact: A validated batch passes if reader-wrong items stay within 1 in 4 of the checked items, for example C302 with 1 wrong of 4. Judgement calls such as the release-repo convention and an unverifiable spec claim decide pass or fail, so they should be recorded explicitly. Verdicts: validated-pass 189, accepted 147, split 18 at progress 336/570.

items.topic: Esm2Psm DUAL mode inconsistent between entry points
items.fact: `Esm2Psm` falls back to ETL for DUAL mode, but `Esm2PsmWork` routes DUAL to Zeta. Expected: consistent behaviour.

items.topic: Esm2Psm trace save, stream leaks and stale registration
items.fact: `save()` skips writing only when trace == null, and the ETL path always passes a non-null map, so an empty trace is still written. `fromModelsAndTrace(File)` and `save(File)` never close their streams. `Esm2Psm` has no try/finally around executeProgram/close. `Esm2PsmTransformationService.uninstall` never removes the model from its registration map.

items.topic: transferObjectType.etl generateBehaviours guard
items.claim: The doc says the whole family of rules is generateBehaviours-guarded.
items.fact: `CreateQueryOrderingType`, `CreateQueryFilterType`, `CreateQuerySeekingType`, the get-range input rules and `CreateUploadTokenType` have no such guard.

items.topic: Script2Operation: Zeta is a stub, bundle location collision, uninstall leak
items.claim: The script2operation AGENTS.md lists an EPSILON mode.
items.fact: No EPSILON mode exists. `Script2OperationZeta` always throws UnsupportedOperationException, and `Script2OperationWork` falls back to ETL, so the ZETA default is effectively ETL and DUAL only closes the Zeta result. `Script2OperationService.install` uses `this.getClass().getName()` as the bundle location for every model, so a second model may collide. `uninstall` never removes the map entry.

items.topic: DefaultWorkflowMojo useCache and null-trace NPE
items.claim: DefaultWorkflowMojo.AGENTS.md: the field initializer wins over the annotation default for `useCache`.
items.fact: `useCache` has `defaultValue="false"` in the annotation but `true` in the field initializer. Maven injects the annotation default, so the effective value is probably false. With `asm` set and `psm2AsmTrace` unset, `ignorePsm2AsmTrace` defaults to true, so the code calls `getArtifact(null)` and throws an NPE. The same happens for `measure` with `psm2MeasureTrace` (lines ~441 and ~451).
items.evidence: batch C378, from reading the code only

items.topic: tatami user guide pages/index.adoc mismatches code
items.claim: The user guide pages/index.adoc gives defaults and names for the Maven plugin.
items.fact: It disagrees with the code on: the `saveModels` default (the code says true); the `destination` default; keycloak versus Measure; `rdbmsColumnNameMaxSize` (the code has `rdbmsColumnMaxNameSize`); and Java 1.8 (the code needs 21).

items.topic: Asm2Keycloak ETL realm.etl does not trim realm names
items.fact: `realm.etl:7` neither trims realm names nor skips blank ones, while the Zeta `RealmRules` does both. A realm annotated ' realm1' is created under a name the client rule never finds, so clients are silently dropped on the ETL path. Also: `ClientRules.java:188` returns an orphan binding when the client equivalent is missing. The Asm2KeycloakTransformationTrace 1024-byte mark can be exceeded by leading whitespace, which makes `reset()` fail. Streams are not closed (lines 271 and 381). `Asm2KeycloakTransformationSerivce` (sic) leaves a stale map entry after uninstall. The ETL and Zeta engines write different XMI IDs for clients (client.etl:20 vs ClientRules.java:124).

items.topic: Asm2Keycloak AGENTS.md claims
items.claim: ClientRules.java.AGENTS.md says `createKeycloakClientClaim` reads `keycloakResource`. Asm2Keycloak.java.AGENTS.md claims MD5 keying for script URIs. Asm2KeycloakRuleNames AGENTS.md says `CreateRealm` is an ETL rule name.
items.fact: All three claims are wrong. The code does not read `keycloakResource` there, does no MD5 keying, and `realm.etl` has no `CreateRealm` rule.

items.topic: asm2rdbms excelToRules.etl cascade and junction primary key
items.claim: asm/reference.eol ruleMapping() row: requires exactly one Rules root.
items.fact: The code takes `RDBMS!Rules.all.first` and never checks the count. `excelToRules.etl:42` reads `cascade` from the target (`t.cascade = t.cascade.asBoolean()`) instead of `s.cascade`, so the spreadsheet column never reaches the model. `reference.etl:96` uses `<= 0` for choosing the junction-table main side, while `isFirst()` in reference.eol uses `< 0`. For equal names both ends claim the junction, so no junction primary key is created. Also: `attribute.eol` uses DOMAIN_* names only when columnPrefix is empty, and the `util.eol` size accessors read injected context variables, not ETL program parameters.

items.topic: asm2rdbms zeta rules AGENTS.md counts and perf test sizes
items.claim: zeta/rules/AGENTS.md:8: 'ten eClassToTable*Field rules'. The perf test sizes are 10/50/100.
items.fact: ClassRules.java has nine eClassToTable*Field rules plus eClassToRdbmsTable, ten @TransformRule methods in total. The perf test sizes in code are 100/500/1000. In `ReferenceRules.java:558`, `fk2.setSqlName` runs only if the source table and PK exist, but fk2 is still added to the junction table and traced, so its sqlName may be null with no warning.

items.topic: psm2asm OperationRules documentation annotation for bound input parameter
items.fact: `OperationRules.java:1831` `createDocumentationAnnotationForBoundInputParameter` looks up `ctx.equivalent(s, EParameter.class)` with s a BoundOperation, but the EParameter is created at line 370 keyed by `s.getInput()` (a Parameter). The key mismatch makes eParam usually null, so the annotation lands on the EOperation instead of the EParameter. ETL (operation.etl:41-46) attaches it to the parameter. Needs a test. Also: `StaticNavigation` extends ReferenceAccessor, not NavigationProperty, so DerivedRules does not process it twice; `StaticData` is a subtype of PrimitiveAccessor.

items.topic: psm2measure and rdbms2liquibase issues
items.claim: AGENTS rows: Psm2MeasureTransformationTrace has a `resolvePsm2MeasureTrace(ResourceSet, URI)` overload; Psm2MeasureWork registers the trace when requested; Psm2MeasureZetaTransformation calls `TransformationExecutor.execute()`; dataUpdateBeforeIncremental.etl covers merge/split migrations.
items.fact: All four rows are wrong. The overload does not exist, the trace is always put into the context, the code calls `executor.transform()`, and the file has no merge/split migrations. Probable bugs: `main.egl:12` takes the backup table name from `op.table` but the data and file name from `op.previousTable`, while the backup, checkup and drop modules use previousTable. `dbCheckup.etl:32` does not abbreviate or upper-case the backup-existence name as creation and drop do, so long table names are checked under a name that is never created. `Psm2MeasureTransformationService.java:97` uninstall does not remove the key from the registration map.

items.topic: Test fixture bugs in judo-ng test utils
items.claim: util/AGENTS.md row lists remove(String). AllTypeOfTransferObjectsModel/.../transfer/AGENTS.md names the model AllTypeOfTransferObjectsModel.
items.fact: The real method is `remove(Map<String,String>)`. The model name in code is "AllTypeOfTransferObjects". `YugabytedbSQLContainer.getLivenessCheckPortNumbers()` calls `new HashSet<>(int)`, so it returns an empty set. `JudoRuntimeFixture` ignores its context map (`requireNonNullElse(null, ...)` always passes a fresh map). The afterEach commit in `JudoDatasourceSingletonExtension` and `JudoRuntimeExtension` swallows exceptions in an empty catch block.

items.topic: judo-ng-read validator rulings (Maven, AsmValidator, JclParser)
items.fact: Validators ruled these reader claims as not bugs. `Eclipse-BundleShape: dir` still builds a JAR. In about.properties, `{featureVersion}` and 'Build id: {0}' are standard Eclipse placeholders. `removeListenerObject` is inherited from Eclipse's EventManager, but the call never removes the editor listeners, so that bug is real. `flatten-maven-plugin` `updatePomFile=true` does not rewrite pom.xml but writes `.flattened-pom.xml`. All CI workflows use Java 17. The esmjql.evl two-way relation check needs no stored/transient guard, because ESM validation (TwoWayRelationMemberValidations.java:61) requires two-way relations to be stored. AsmValidator registers no rules on purpose, since asm.evl is empty. `getBaseDurationRatio` converts to the unit base deliberately. The wrong number is in the spec. Spec `java-validation` claims a work-stealing pool for parallel validation. This repo only passes the `parallel` flag to judo-zeta, so it is unverified. The sample .jcl/.xmi tests live under model-test/src/test/model/. JclParser's second resource set gives the same default load options.
